judgements.reason: Compact groups is already in the baseline end to end - TauCeti.peterWeylBasis with IsIrrepSkeleton, Schur orthogonality, the convolution/approximate-identity density proof and TauCeti.characterBasis are all present and sorry-free - so almost no new theory is needed; AlgebraicCurves still has to build the cotrace and the Hurwitz genus formula, constant-field extensions with genus invariance, Hilbert's different formula, local expansions and residues with the Delta_F = Omega_F comparison, the hyperelliptic and plane-curve genus formulas, Weierstrass points and the 84(g-1) bound, and the whole Layer-12 function-field/curve anti-equivalence.

Both are about half built, but AlgebraicCurves has more left in absolute terms: its Layers 7-12 add the cotrace and Hurwitz formula, constant-field extension theory with the inseparable genus drop, residues and the comparison theorem, model classes with Kummer and Artin-Schreier genus formulas, Weierstrass points and automorphism finiteness, and a five-part scheme dictionary (normalization of P^1_k in F, the anti-equivalence, and the coherent-cohomology comparison), whereas LocalFieldsRamification's remainder - the finite-extension valuative package with e and f, unramified extensions and Frobenius, the lower/upper ramification filtration with Herbrand, Hasse-Arf, the different, and the tame quotient with the Iwasawa presentation - is one classical chapter (Serre LF) plus profinite Sylow/free-profinite inputs.

ClassFieldTheory imports exactly the part of LocalFieldsRamification that is missing (Frobenius and the unramified norm groups for the local invariant, the ramification filtration for solvability of local Galois groups, the different for conductors) and then stacks thirteen further unbuilt layers on it - Tate cup products, class formations and fundamental classes, Tate's theorem, the abstract Artin map, the Brauer invariant and local duality, local reciprocity and existence, the Weil group, the Brauer sum-of-invariants sequence with the two fundamental inequalities, global reciprocity and existence, ray and Hilbert class fields, Kronecker-Weber - and additionally needs GlobalNumberFields' ideles, moduli and ray class groups, which are essentially unbuilt.

ReductiveGroups already has Layers 0-6 in the baseline (Hopf/affine-group-scheme anti-equivalence, the embedding theorem, Tannaka, tori and character lattices, unipotent radical, reductivity, Borel and maximal-torus existence) and needs three further layers: conjugacy plus root data, Bruhat/BN-pairs, the classification and Chevalley existence, and the pinned Chevalley-Demazure Z-forms with their special isogenies. ClassFieldTheory has only its cohomology suppliers and Layer 1 formations, leaving thirteen layers spanning local and global class field theory plus an unbuilt idele/ray-class substrate from GlobalNumberFields, which is both more theory and a deeper stack.

AutomorphicLFunctions needs the reductive-group theory that ReductiveGroups is still missing (through AdelicAlgebraicGroups and ReductiveGroupsPartII) and then, on top of it, whole bodies of theory absent from both libraries: smooth admissible representations of p-adic groups with Jacquet modules, the Satake isomorphism, Whittaker models and Bernstein-Zelevinsky derivatives; real reductive (g,K)-module theory with Casselman-Wallach globalization; adelic Schwartz-Bruhat spaces and Poisson summation; and then Tate, Godement-Jacquet and Rankin-Selberg zeta integrals with their epsilon and gamma factors.

Both sit on large unbuilt towers, but ModularSymbols stacks more of them: its targets need modular symbols and Eichler-Shimura at general level, integral period lattices, distribution-valued symbols with Stevens control, and the critical-slope constructions, which pull LocallyAnalyticDistributions, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras, DirichletPadicLFunctions and PadicFamilies' eigenvarieties, and through PadicFamilies the algebraic modular-curve tower with integral Hecke correspondences (52 upstream stages over 14 roadmaps, depth 12). AutomorphicLFunctions' chain is heavier per stage but narrower - reductive groups, smooth p-adic and real reductive representation theory, adelic analysis, then the zeta integrals (19 upstream stages over 6 roadmaps, depth 5).

ModularSymbols only needs the modular-curve tower up to the algebraic Hecke correspondences, and can take its L0-L2 through the analytic carrier; ModularCurvesPartII must build that tower and then everything past it - bad fibres and regular/semistable models, Jacobians with integral Hecke actions, integral etale and Betti parabolic cohomology with Poincare duality, Ihara's lemma with integral saturation and the modular abelian variety A_f - which drags in Neron models, etale duality and perverse sheaves, weights and nearby cycles (56 upstream stages plus 20 of its own, against ModularSymbols' 57 total).

StableReduction is deep but self-contained: its missing layers are coherent cohomology with base change, dualizing sheaves, relative Proj and ampleness, nodal curves and dual graphs, blowups and arithmetic-surface intersection theory, minimal models, semistable reduction and stabilization, all over a DVR, with Layers 0 and 6 already started in the baseline. ModularCurvesPartII needs its own semistable-model theory for modular curves and, on top of that, algebraic stacks and coarse spaces, generalised elliptic curves and Tate curves, abelian schemes, Neron models, complex GAGA/Chow/de Rham comparisons and integral etale cohomology with duality - 14 upstream roadmaps, none of them started.

StableReduction builds curve theory directly on Mathlib's scheme language, and Mathlib already supplies Proj, normalization, valuative criteria and the Rees algebra. HodgeTate has to stand on perfectoid spaces, adic spaces and diamonds, relative p-adic Hodge theory with period sheaves, crystalline and prismatic cohomology, abelian schemes and p-divisible groups, and the entire Shimura-variety tower with its compactifications and automorphic bundles, before proving canonical subgroups with quantitative radii and the logarithmic Riemann-Hilbert comparison of Diao-Lan-Liu-Zhu - 196 upstream stages over 35 roadmaps, of which the libraries contain only the Fontaine theta map and the first steps of Spa.

The two share the perfectoid/diamond/etale-cohomology substrate, but HodgeTate needs that substrate and the whole Shimura programme on top of it - ShimuraData, PELModuli, ShimuraVarieties, ShimuraCompactifications, HilbertModularVarieties and AutomorphicBundles, plus crystalline and A_inf cohomology - before its own canonical-subgroup and logarithmic-period work, while LanglandsParameterStacks needs derived algebraic geometry, the Weil group and integral reductive invariant theory but no Shimura variety or crystalline comparison (196 upstream stages over 35 roadmaps against 112 over 24).

LanglandsParameterStacks needs the diamond/derived-geometry substrate plus the Weil group and integral invariant theory (112 upstream stages over 24 roadmaps); OrdinaryAutomorphicForms needs the algebraic modular-curve and Hilbert-modular towers, automorphic Galois representations, local and global Galois deformation rings, Taylor-Wiles patching and Hida families, and through the Galois-representation supplier much of the same perfectoid and p-adic Hodge stack as well (394 upstream stages over 62 roadmaps, depth 19).

PotentialModularity consumes OrdinaryAutomorphicForms R21.6 as an input, so its missing theory strictly contains that roadmap's, and it adds Moret-Bailly's rational-point theorem, the twisted Hilbert-Blumenthal torsion moduli problem with geometric irreducibility, potential residual modularity, KW's global finiteness and prescribed-lift constructions and the compatible-systems machinery, together with the full Taylor-Wiles R = T theorem of GL2ModularityLifting and the Jacquet-Langlands/solvable base change of GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.

ShimuraVarieties is itself very far - Baily-Borel, Borel algebraicity, the main theorem of complex multiplication, Milne's conjugation and descent, plus class field theory - but it is 69 upstream stages over 21 roadmaps; PotentialModularity has 429 upstream stages over 65 roadmaps, includes eight ShimuraVarieties stages among them, and then needs modularity lifting, Galois deformation theory, patching, potential residual modularity and compatible systems on top.

Compact groups is finished in the baseline: TauCeti.peterWeylBasis, the Schur orthogonality relations, the convolution-operator density argument and TauCeti.characterBasis are all present and sorry-free, so its remaining work is packaging. LocalFieldsRamification still has to build the finite-extension valuative package with e and f, the deep-unit logarithm, unramified extensions with Frobenius and Gal(K^ur/K) = Zhat, Eisenstein/tame/wild theory, the lower and upper ramification filtrations with the Herbrand functions, Hasse-Arf, the different and discriminant, and the tame quotient with its Iwasawa presentation.

Close: ShimuraVarieties must prove Baily-Borel and Borel algebraicity, the main theorem of complex multiplication and Milne's conjugation/descent, and it consumes the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap, itself thirteen unbuilt layers deep. LanglandsParameterStacks needs a wider unbuilt base - derived algebraic geometry with animated rings and perfect complexes, quotient stacks and GIT, the diamond/v-stack sheaf theory, condensed cocycles and the local Weil group, and integral Weyl/dual-Weyl module theory with Donkin's property - 112 upstream stages over 24 roadmaps against 69 over 21, which I judge to outweigh the class-field-theory import on the other side.

ModularSymbols needs the p-adic analytic tower (distributions, Iwasawa algebras, eigenvarieties) over the algebraic modular curves: 52 upstream stages over 14 roadmaps. PotentialModularity needs all of that indirectly plus Galois deformation theory, Taylor-Wiles patching, automorphic Galois representations, Hilbert-Blumenthal moduli, Moret-Bailly, solvable base change and the KW lifting interface: 429 upstream stages over 65 roadmaps, depth 16.

The hardest pair in this block. StableReduction's missing Layer 2 - coherent pushforward with cohomology and base change, Grauert, relative dualizing sheaves, relative Proj and polarized etale descent - is absent from both libraries and carries a nine-deep serial chain up to stabilization and stable maps. But ClassFieldTheory has more theory left and stacks it at least as deep: thirteen unbuilt layers from Tate cup products and class formations through Tate's theorem, the Artin map, the local Brauer invariant with Kummer theory and local duality, local reciprocity, existence and the Weil group, the global Brauer sequence with both fundamental inequalities, global reciprocity and existence, ray/Hilbert/ring class fields and Kronecker-Weber - and it additionally imports the unbuilt Layers 2-4 of LocalFieldsRamification, where StableReduction's only external import (the JacobianChallenge Pic^0 contracts) is already partly built.

ReductiveGroups has Layers 0-6 in the baseline and needs three more - conjugacy and root data, the classification with Chevalley existence, and the pinned Chevalley-Demazure Z-forms. ModularCurvesPartII has nothing built (the audit finds no modular curve in either library in any form) and needs twenty of its own stages plus 56 upstream stages over 14 roadmaps: algebraic stacks and coarse spaces, generalised elliptic curves, abelian schemes, Neron models, GAGA and Chow algebraization, integral etale cohomology with duality, and semistable models.

AutomorphicLFunctions needs a deep but narrow chain - reductive groups, adelic measures, smooth p-adic and real reductive representation theory, then Tate/Godement-Jacquet/Rankin-Selberg zeta integrals (19 upstream stages over 6 roadmaps). ShimuraVarieties needs abelian schemes with PEL structures, algebraic moduli with coarse spaces and a resolution input, complex GAGA and Chow, reduction theory for arithmetic groups, and then must prove Baily-Borel, Borel algebraicity, the main theorem of complex multiplication and Milne's conjugation/descent, while also consuming the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap for the reflex-norm reciprocity condition (69 upstream stages over 21 roadmaps plus that import).

HodgeTate needs the perfectoid/diamond/p-adic-Hodge stack and the Shimura tower (196 upstream stages over 35 roadmaps). OrdinaryAutomorphicForms needs much of that same stack through its automorphic Galois representation supplier and adds the algebraic modular-curve and Hilbert-modular towers with their integral Hecke modules, local and global Galois deformation rings, Taylor-Wiles patching, Hida families and the Skinner-Wiles residually reducible arguments (394 upstream stages over 62 roadmaps, depth 19).

AlgebraicCurves has more layers left, but they are a textbook completion on a base that already contains Riemann-Roch, duality, the different with its tame value and the ramification groups: Hurwitz, constant-field extensions, residues, model classes, Weierstrass points and the curve dictionary. ReductiveGroups' three remaining layers are the deep end of the subject with no formalized precedent - Borel and maximal-torus conjugacy and the root datum of a split pair, then Bruhat/BN-pairs and the relative theory, then the isomorphism and existence theorems classifying split reductive groups by root data, and finally the explicit Chevalley-Demazure construction over Z via Chevalley bases and the Kostant Z-form with its pinnings, commutator relations and the special isogenies in characteristics two and three.

LanglandsParameterStacks needs derived algebraic geometry, the local Weil group, the cocycle stack and integral reductive invariant theory on the diamond/etale substrate (112 upstream stages over 24 roadmaps). PotentialModularity needs the algebraic modular-curve and Hilbert-modular towers, automorphic Galois representations, local and global deformation rings, Taylor-Wiles patching, ordinary modularity lifting, solvable base change, Moret-Bailly and the KW compatible-systems machinery (429 upstream stages over 65 roadmaps).

ClassFieldTheory has thirteen unbuilt layers, but their substrate is in comparatively good shape - Tate and continuous cohomology with restriction, corestriction and cup products, the Formation/NormalLayer framework, Mathlib's idele class group and Tau Ceti's ray class groups with moduli are all present - so the missing work, though very large, is one coherent arithmetic body. ModularSymbols needs modular symbols and Eichler-Shimura, integral periods, locally analytic distributions with Stevens control and the critical-slope eigenvariety constructions, and these rest on areas absent from both libraries altogether: algebraic stacks and coarse moduli, abelian schemes, generalised elliptic curves with integral Hecke correspondences, GAGA, and rigid-analytic eigenvarieties - 52 upstream stages over 14 roadmaps at depth 12.

LocalFieldsRamification is one classical chapter away from completion: the finite-extension valuative package, unramified extensions with Frobenius, the ramification filtration with Herbrand and Hasse-Arf, the different, and the tame quotient, on a base that already has the normalized valuation, the unit filtration and Teichmuller. AutomorphicLFunctions needs all of reductive group structure theory, adelic measures and reduction theory, smooth admissible representations of p-adic groups with Satake and Whittaker models, real reductive (g,K)-module theory with Casselman-Wallach, and only then its own Schwartz-Bruhat, Tate, Godement-Jacquet and Rankin-Selberg theory.
